issues.description: Function parameter mismatch for simulate_msd_two_rounds: the problem statement documents the function as simulate_msd_two_rounds(n_shots: int, p: float, batch_size: float = 1000000.0) -> tuple[float, float], while both the template implementation (msd.py) and the reference solution implement the function as simulate_msd_two_rounds(n_shots: int, p: float, batch_size: int = 1000000) -> tuple[float, float]. This discrepancy is specifically about the type and default of the batch_size parameter (float vs int) and may confuse students about whether batch_size should be an integer count of shots per batch or a floating-point value.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the batch_size parameter consistent across all artifacts. Prefer treating batch_size as an integer number of shots per batch: update the problem statement signature to simulate_msd_two_rounds(n_shots: int, p: float, batch_size: int = 1000000) -> tuple[float, float] and add a short sentence explaining that batch_size is the integer number of shots processed per simulation batch. Alternatively, if a float was intentional, change the template and solution signatures and defaults to use batch_size: float and document how non-integer values are interpreted (e.g., rounded or cast to int) — but using an int is recommended for clarity.
